transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-12
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~1:08
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CS), Hannah (Larkspur Dir Platform), Omar (Larkspur SRE), Lisa (Larkspur Head ML), Devon (Larkspur Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving time, I'm Jordan from Redwood, really quick intro round before we dive, ethan you wanna kick off with the tech scope?
[00:12] Ethan: yeah, sure. thanks jordan. hey hannah, omar, lisa, devon. quick high level — this call is to align on the private deployment checklist and lock the first sprint commitments. we'll cover bench plan, network, kms, and acceptance criteria.
[00:30] Hannah: sounds good. big thing for us is we need predictable latency for our storefront autosuggest, target p95 is 120ms under peak, and we want to avoid big cost surprises.
[00:42] Omar: and from infra side we need VPC peering options, egress rules, and a runbook for failover. also want to confirm if we can run the service in our AZs for data residency.
[00:55] Jordan: totally. priya will be primary CS for the engagement and ethan is SE lead. priya, quick note on timelines?
[01:05] Priya: hi all. we typically do a 6-week ramp: week 0-1 prep (network + access + keys), week 2 deploy + smoke tests, week 3 canary load, weeks 4-6 tuning and handoff. we can compress if procurement is ready sooner.
[01:19] Devon: procurement here — typical timeline is 2 weeks once PO is issued, but we need contract language for data residency and indemnity. can you flag any unusual clauses?
[01:30] Jordan: we can send the standard enterprise addendum. priya will drop the contract owner and cs legal contact.
[01:35] Lisa: from model side, we plan to start with the medium LLM variant for latency/cost tradeoff. question: does Redwood support automatic fallback to smaller quantized model on overload?
[01:48] Ethan: yes, we have routing policies — it's called a model-variant fallback policy in the console. sometimes the transcript accidentally calls it 'fallback pipe' — but we'll share the config. fallback keeps semantics but reduces cost.
[02:02] Hannah: good. also want to confirm KV cache behavior — we rely on prefix caching for the chat flows. anything special for private?
[02:12] Ethan: KV cache is supported; in private there are options for in-memory or on-disk persistence depending on restart policies. note: there can be cold starts on pod restarts so we recommend warmup routines.
[02:26] Omar: network — do you need a public IP? can we do NAT only?
[02:31] Jordan: NAT-only is fine, we support private peering via transit gateway or direct connect. we'll share network diagrams.
[02:40] [05:00] Hannah: (interrupting) sorry, quick sidebar — our security team will need SOC2 headers, encryption at rest details, KMS flow, and audit log retention periods.
[05:10] Priya: we're SOC2 certified, and we have an ISO summary. I'll share the SOC2 summary and the audit log retention options. for KMS we integrate with customer KMS through HSM-backed keys in the private plane — sorry private plane? private control plane, bit of a mouthful — but yes, customer keys are supported.
[06:00] Ethan: small note on perf tests: to reproduce your p95 120ms we need representative traces, including token lengths and prompt templates. if you can provide those we can run the canary with your workload.
[06:18] Lisa: we have a mix — queries averaging 18 tokens and some outliers at 256 for long form recommendations. we'll pull a sample.
[06:30] Omar: i'll extract traces but need to mask PII, do you have guidance?
[06:36] Priya: yes, we have a small script for redaction, ethan will post it.
[06:45] Jordan: for acceptance criteria, can we agree on these: 1) p95 under canary within 15% of target, 2) no errors above 0.5% for request rate during the canary window, 3) cost per 1k tokens within expected band that we define?
[07:05] Hannah: yes that works, we want written thresholds.
[07:12] Devon: procurement will gate on max month-1 spend estimate, can you provide a delta range?
[07:18] Ethan: we'll run cost projection with your traffic profile; results next week.
[07:25] [15:00] Jordan: ok logistics — iam and SSO: do you use okta or azure ad?
[15:07] Omar: okta.
[15:09] Priya: we support SAML SSO with Okta and can set up SCIM for user provisioning.
[15:15] Lisa: about model versioning — we want the ability to pin versions during the canary and then do A/B. is that in the console?
[15:22] Ethan: yes, rollout features include canary and A/B toggles. we'll demo in the week-2 deploy if you want.
[15:30] Hannah: question on observability retention — we have compliance constraints to keep logs for 3 years, is that possible?
[15:38] Jordan: built-in retention default is 90 days but enterprise add-on can extend. priya will share options and pricing.
[15:46] Devon: that pricing will be in the contract appendix right?
[15:50] Priya: yes.
[25:00] Hannah: ok let's talk canary window — we're thinking a 2-hour window in a low traffic period but with replayed peak traffic. is that doable?
[25:12] Ethan: yes, we can replay traces to emulate peak. note that continuous batching optimization will change latencies slightly versus single-request flow. we'll document the difference.
[25:30] Omar: any pre-reqs on the Larkspur side for the canary?
[25:35] Ethan: access to the workload traces, VPN/VPC peering in place, KMS keys provisioned, and a user to run the smoke script.
[25:45] Jordan: on security we will provide a network diagram and the HSM/KMS integration docs.
[25:55] Lisa: when we hand off to our platform team, who is the on-call?
[26:00] Priya: during onboarding Redwood provides a 2-week high-touch support window and a named CSM (me). we also assign an engineering owner (ethan) for canary support. after SLA go-live we transition to standard on-call.
[26:15] Devon: procurement question again: if we need an on-prem air-gapped package is that offered?
[26:22] Jordan: we do have an on-prem option but it's a separate engagement; we can outline differences now and decide later.
[30:00] [35:00] Ethan: i'm going to summarize the benchmark script — it's a small load generator that hits endpoints with your prompt templates, measures token-level latency and success rate. i'll push it to the shared drive and include a README.
[35:20] Hannah: great, can you also include the cost-estimator template?
[35:25] Ethan: yes.
[35:30] Priya: action items recap — I'll enumerate in the email but high level: security docs, benchmark script, workload traces, procurement timeline.
[35:40] Jordan: do we want to set the follow-up for next tuesday?
[35:45] Hannah: tuesday the 20th works for a 30-minute tech sync.
[35:50] Devon: yes please include procurement stakeholders.
[36:00] [55:00] Lisa: small nit — when we talk about quantization, what level do you support? 4-bit? 8-bit?
[55:10] Ethan: currently we support int8 and experimental int4 paths depending on model architecture. we'll recommend profile per workload.
[55:20] Omar: any known gotchas running behind our firewall?
[55:26] Ethan: sometimes TLS termination and large payloads require tuning of the ingress gateway; we'll share recommended nginx/ALB settings.
[55:35] Hannah: ok i'm comfortable with the plan.
[55:40] Jordan: great. final recap of next steps and owners — (priya list) 1) priya to share SOC2, ISO summary & network diagram 2) ethan to post benchmark script and cost estimator 3) omar to upload redacted traces 4) devon to confirm procurement timeline. We'll meet 2027-04-20 10:00 PT for the tech check-in.
[57:00] Devon: thanks all. one last ask — can you include a short checklist for our security review to hand to legal?
[57:12] Priya: yes i'll include a 1-page checklist with exact artifact names.
[57:20] Jordan: awesome, thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

Notes / Links mentioned: shared drive link (will be posted) - benchmark script, SOC2 summary, network diagram, cost-estimator template.

End of transcript.
